questions.q: How does this lesson frame the relationship between consulting and in-house ServiceNow careers?
options: Consulting is strictly the more serious, advanced path and in-house is a fallback
In-house is always a stepping stone toward eventually becoming a consultant
They're two structurally different, equally legitimate career paths with real tradeoffs, not a better-and-worse pair
Only consulting work leads anywhere toward CTA candidacy
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly presents both as legitimate, structurally different paths, not a hierarchy.

questions.q: What is the concrete upside of consulting work that this lesson highlights?
options: Guaranteed higher pay in every case
Exposure to a wider variety of instances, industries, and architecture decisions in a shorter span of time, because each engagement differs
No project deadlines or client pressure of any kind
Permanent, single-client assignments with no travel
questions.explain: Moving between client engagements exposes a consultant to varied CMDB structures, integration landscapes, and governance constraints relatively quickly.

questions.q: What is the concrete upside of in-house work that this lesson highlights?
options: Depth — living with the long-term consequences of architecture and configuration decisions in one complex environment, plus generally higher day-to-day predictability
Constant travel to new client sites
A new employer every few months
No need to ever understand the organization's own instance history
questions.explain: In-house roles trade breadth for depth: deep, long-term familiarity with one instance and typically more predictable day-to-day work.

questions.q: According to this lesson, does either path "win" the question of building CTA-relevant readiness faster?
options: Yes, consulting always wins because it has more client variety
Yes, in-house always wins because of long-term depth
No — what matters is whether the day-to-day work includes real architectural decision-making, not which structural category the employer falls into
Neither path can ever build CTA-relevant experience
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly rejects a single right answer, framing the substance of the work as what actually matters, not the structural category.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend evaluating when weighing a consulting offer against an in-house offer?
options: Only the company's brand recognition
The actual substance of the work — whether it includes real architecture decision-making — plus honest personal factors like travel tolerance and appetite for variety versus depth
Whichever option pays slightly more in year one, regardless of role content
Whichever title sounds more senior on a business card
questions.explain: The lesson recommends asking about actual work substance and weighing honest personal circumstances, not picking based on prestige alone.
